correctness.rationale: Geodesic distance is minimized by the nearest horizontal deck translate, with all candidate upper semicircle geodesics staying in the truncated cusp. Independent Exp(1) heights imply independent \(S\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)\) and \(T\sim\operatorname{Exp}(2)\), while nearest angular displacement is uniform. The independent product W^2e^{-2T} has survival \((1-\sqrt z)^2\), giving the exact formula. A near-r boundary layer u=O_lambda(e^-2r) yields a rigorous \(\lambda^2e^{-3r}/24\) correction with \(O_\lambda(e^{-5r})\) error. The monotone coupling yields strict stochastic order. Executed standalone checks corroborate formulas but are not proofs.

value.rationale: A finite-area noncompact metric cusp is a canonical geometric end. The full random-pair distance law yields an explicit, nontrivial product factorization, a universally shared leading exponential tail and the first coefficient that identifies the boundary horocycle length. Exact first-order stochastic ordering provides a global comparison, making this a natural inverse-distance and random-geometry result beyond simple sample averages.
